questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to outside Europe in a country that has a lot of different things to offer and a great university. Furthermore i like the Australian culture and the weather is great ;)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the best exchange experience. I am so glad i went so Australia and especially Sydney. I met a lot of amazing new people who are now my close friends and the country is amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The university of Sydney is great at guiding you. I had an exchange mentor who sent us email with the things we needed to do and was really helpful guiding us through the whole semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was introduction days and emails sent out all the time of what to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is hard. You need to spend some time on it. I found an apartment outside the university after ca. one week in Australia. I found it with three other girls from Denmark. But the university do offer housing on campus if you dont want to find something yourself. I really liked living off tho and enjoyed the area we stayed at.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living both on and off campus is expensive. A lot of Danish students lived in the on campus housing but i really enjoyed living off campus with three friends in a nice area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good at guiding us but there is a lot you need to fill out.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They send you links end emails on how to do it through their website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Yes, you have your own counselor signed to you that you can write if you have any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted at the first try. And they sent out an excel ark of all the classes that are available to take for exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I find that they were more things to do through the semester but that level was lower than i Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Is is different from UCPH. It is more like gymnasium. You need to do a lot of smaller assignments and quizzes that all adds up to your grade, and some courses you also need to show up to since they take attendance in some courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: Not unexpected but I traveled a lot and traveling to different cities in Australia is quite cheap. But in general, the prices in Australia are the same as in Denmark. The housing prices are a bit more expensive though.

questions.answer: A lot! There are more than hundreds of different clubs and athletic activities.

What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Kangaroo Island, east-coast roadtrip, exploring Sydney and Bondi beach (love Surry Hills and Darlinghurst).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - Australians are open and sweet.
